title: Streaming standby on PostgreSQL 16.14 stops applying WAL at MultiXactOffsetSLRU when primary is 16.8
body: I accidentally ran a PostgreSQL 16.14 physical streaming standby against a 16.8 primary on Ubuntu 22.04. WAL continues to arrive and receive/write/flush stay current, but replay stops and the lag grows to about 9 GB. The standby startup process repeatedly reports wait_event_type = LWLock and wait_event = MultiXactOffsetSLRU and is parked in futex_wait_queue. After resetting pg_stat_slru and waiting 60 seconds under live streaming, both MultiXactMember and MultiXactOffset show zero reads, writes, hits, or zeroed blocks. The replay LSN remains frozen while the receive LSN advances. There are no hot-standby readers, MultiXact ages on the primary are small, and the other 16.8 replicas are unaffected. Restarting clears the block temporarily, but it recurs after catch-up. Downgrading this standby to 16.12 with the same data directory initially restored normal replay.

symptoms_visible: My 16.14 standby keeps receiving WAL from the 16.8 primary, but its replay LSN remains frozen and the locally buffered WAL grows to about 9 GB.
The startup process remains parked in futex_wait_queue with wait_event LWLock:MultiXactOffsetSLRU, while the MultiXact SLRU counters stay at zero.
Restarting lets replay catch up temporarily, but the same stall returns.
N0.label: N0 cross-minor standby replay stall reported

symptoms_visible: With the standby pinned to 16.12, replay initially runs normally, but after more than 12 hours recovery terminates with 'could not access status of transaction' and a short read from pg_multixact/offsets/017C during MultiXact CREATE_ID redo.
N1_x.label: N1_x downgrade workaround aftermath

symptoms_visible: The affected startup process is still blocked on the MultiXactOffsetSLRU lock while replaying a MultiXact CREATE_ID record.
N1.label: N1 startup backtrace and WAL record collected

symptoms_visible: In a fresh 16.8-primary and 16.14-standby test, the unpatched startup process blocks when the MultiXact offsets page boundary is crossed, while the candidate-patched standby replays all WAL and catches up.
N2.label: N2 candidate patch verified in cross-version replay test

symptoms_visible: A separate cross-version test standby catches up with the patch, and maintainers report that the change has been applied to the affected branches.
I have not yet retested a build containing the applied fix on my original standby.
N_terminal.label: terminal fix applied but original reporter has not retested

question_patterns: Can you capture a debugger backtrace of the hanging startup process using debug symbols?
Please attach gdb to the blocked startup process and show the complete call stack.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The backtrace ends in PGSemaphoreLock, then LWLockAcquire in exclusive mode, SimpleLruWriteAll with MultiXactOffsetCtl, RecordNewMultiXact, multixact_redo, ApplyWalRecord, and PerformWalRecovery.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The complete backtrace never enters MultiXact redo or SimpleLruWriteAll; it is waiting in an extension callback during recovery.
The same frames and arguments appear, but the libc semaphore frames have different addresses because this host uses another Ubuntu package build.

question_patterns: What is the last replayed LSN, and what does pg_waldump show around the record where replay stops?
Can you provide the WAL record immediately around the frozen replay position?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: My WAL dump shows the matching MultiXact CREATE_ID record: multi 79871, offset 218449, nmembers 2. The debugger shows RecordNewMultiXact handling those same values when it blocks.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The WAL dump at the frozen replay LSN contains only heap and B-tree records and no MultiXact CREATE_ID record.
A different reproduction stops on another CREATE_ID value at the same kind of offsets-page boundary.

edges.comment: Messages c0-c6. The debug backtraces came from participant2 and participant4, and the matching WAL dump came from participant4; these affected installations are folded into the simulated user side. The answers retain the raw stack frames and WAL values. Identifying the same-lock self-deadlock is engineer-side inference.

question_patterns: Can you test the attached candidate patch with an older primary and current standby while generating enough MultiXacts to cross an offsets-page boundary?
Please compare an unpatched and patched standby using the same cross-version WAL workload and report what each one does.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I tested a fresh REL_16_8 primary with a REL_16_14 standby built with assertions and generated about 2300 MultiXacts across the offsets-page boundary. Without the patch, startup deadlocks at RecordNewMultiXact for multi 2047. With the patch, the standby replays all WAL and catches up.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The candidate-patched standby deadlocks at the same record as the unpatched build.
The same comparison succeeds after generating 2500 MultiXacts instead of about 2300.

edges.comment: Messages c13 and c15. Participant1's automated REL_16_0-to-REL_16_STABLE reproduction and participant7's fresh 16.8-to-16.14 test are folded into one measurement result. This is pre-landing candidate-patch verification, so it remains a clarification-only measurement.

solution.intent: Correct the back-branch RecordNewMultiXact locking order by delaying acquisition of the MultiXact offsets SLRU lock until after the compatibility-path pre-work, while retaining the flush-before-physical-page-check behavior, then have the reporter verify replay using a build containing the applied fix.
solution.concrete_example: Change the affected back branches so RecordNewMultiXact performs the earlier compatibility checks before acquiring the MultiXact offsets SLRU lock, matching the newer-branch locking order. Keep the SLRU flush before checking whether the next page exists. After applying the change, replay older-minor WAL containing enough MultiXacts to cross an offsets-page boundary and confirm that the standby catches up.
solution.inference_hint: The backtrace establishes that replay reaches SimpleLruWriteAll from RecordNewMultiXact, but the conclusion that the outer code already owns the same SLRU control lock is engineer analysis. The final accepted fix is not the earlier proposal to remove the flush or release and reacquire the lock; it moves the initial lock acquisition later, matching newer branches while preserving the flush-before-check rule.

edges.comment: Messages c3-c16. Participant3 first identified the same-lock self-deadlock, then withdrew the initial remove-the-flush proposal after participant5 supplied a WAL-ordering counterexample. The final accepted patch from participant1 moves lock acquisition later, was reviewed, tested against cross-version WAL, and applied by participant6 to v14-v16. The original reporter did not subsequently confirm the landed fix on the production standby.

solution.intent: Keep the standby pinned to PostgreSQL 16.12 because that version initially resumes replay against the older primary.
solution.concrete_example: Downgrade only the standby binary to 16.12 and keep using the same data directory while the primary remains on 16.8.

edges.comment: Opening report and c4 from participant4. Pinning 16.12 initially avoids the reported lock stall, but it is not a durable resolution: after more than 12 hours that standby fails recovery on a short read from a pg_multixact offsets file.

solution.intent: Replace the unsafe version-pin workaround with the accepted back-branch locking-order correction, preserve the compatibility flush, and require a retest on a build containing that correction.
solution.concrete_example: Do not treat 16.12 as the permanent fix. Use a build with the corrected RecordNewMultiXact locking order, replay the older primary's WAL through a MultiXact offsets-page boundary, and confirm that recovery catches up without either the LWLock stall or the pg_multixact short-read failure.
solution.inference_hint: This shortcut allows an agent to recover from the demonstrated 16.12 workaround failure by giving the thread's accepted fix directly. It skips the detailed debugger, WAL-dump, and candidate-build measurements.

edges.comment: Recovery edge from the real failed downgrade workaround to the accepted technical resolution. It is a shortcut because the detailed diagnostic and candidate-patch evidence was produced on other affected or dedicated test environments rather than on the downgraded production standby.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the final accepted root cause: during back-branch cross-version MultiXact redo, RecordNewMultiXact already holds the MultiXact offsets SLRU lock when SimpleLruWriteAll attempts to acquire that same control lock, causing the startup process to self-deadlock before any SLRU I/O occurs.

The diagnosis must be grounded in the frozen replay with advancing receive LSN, zero MultiXact SLRU activity, the startup backtrace through SimpleLruWriteAll and RecordNewMultiXact, and the matching MultiXact CREATE_ID WAL record.

Must describe the accepted fix as moving the initial MultiXact offsets SLRU lock acquisition later, consistent with newer branches, while preserving the flush-before-physical-page-check compatibility behavior.
Must not recommend permanently pinning the standby to 16.12: that workaround later failed recovery with a pg_multixact offsets short read.

Must not present removing SimpleLruWriteAll as the fix, because the thread withdrew that approach after identifying WAL orderings where dirty buffered pages must be flushed before the physical-page check.

Must ask the original reporter to retest a build containing the applied fix and confirm that replay catches up before declaring the production incident resolved; separate test and buildfarm success are supporting evidence, not the reporter's own verification.

persona_hint.experience_level: Experienced PostgreSQL operator or DBA who can inspect replication statistics, process wait events, kernel stacks, SLRU counters, WAL positions, debugger backtraces, and pg_waldump output. Additional affected operators and patch testers are folded into the simulated user side.
persona_hint.communication_style: Detailed, evidence-driven, and cooperative. Provides exact versions, SQL observations, stack traces, WAL records, and test results; distinguishes temporary recovery from durable resolution and is willing to build a reproduction harness.
